comments: Novel application of quantum metrology concepts to characterize Kondo destruction critical fluctuations; opens new experimental direction across strange metal platforms.

model_io.model: heavy-fermion strange metal system

hypotheses.hypothesis: Quantum Fisher information characterizes multipartite entanglement underlying strange metal formation
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: QFI increases strongly with decreasing temperature; points to Kondo destruction mechanism

title: Evidence of time-reversal symmetry breaking above the charge density wave order in a kagome metal
task: Evidence time-reversal symmetry breaking and loop-current order in kagome metal CsV3Sb5 above charge density wave transition
key_results: Time-reversal symmetry broken well above CDW ordering temperature; loop-current order confirmed via circular dichroism in ARPES; hierarchy: loop-current → CDW → superconductivity
comments: Momentum-resolved, domain-selective dichroism measurements reveal complex temperature evolution; establishes phase transition hierarchy in kagome metals.

model_io.model: kagome metal CsV3Sb5

hypotheses.hypothesis: Loop-current order breaks time-reversal symmetry above CDW transition temperature
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: dichroic signal observed above CDW ordering; supports loop-current mechanism

title: Orbital Hall conductivity and relaxation in thin films with variable disorder
task: Characterize orbital Hall conductivity and relaxation in disordered to single-crystalline Mn films via orbital Hanle magnetoresistance
key_results: Orbital Hall conductivity scales linearly with electrical conductivity (hopping regime); orbital relaxation ~ps timescale; crossover from orbital dephasing to interorbital hopping with temperature
comments: Establishes orbital angular momentum as structurally resilient degree of freedom; Elliott–Yafet-type scattering dominates in crystalline phase.

model_io.model: Mn thin films (amorphous to single-crystalline α-Mn)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Orbital Hall conductivity scales with electrical conductivity in hopping-dominated regime analogously to spin/anomalous Hall effects
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: linear scaling observed from amorphous to polycrystalline films; distinct relaxation channels identified

title: Strong coupling of a microwave photon to an electron on helium
task: Demonstrate strong cavity QED coupling between microwave photon and electron on superfluid helium
key_results: Strong coupling regime achieved between single photon and quantized electron motional state; enables single-electron spin qubit readout; fidelity >98% predicted
comments: First strong coupling demonstration in electron-on-helium platform using superconducting resonator and quantum dot; establishes foundation for scalable quantum computing.

model_io.model: quantum dot + superconducting resonator coupled to electron on superfluid helium

hypotheses.hypothesis: Strong coupling enables high-fidelity single-shot spin readout via cavity QED
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: predicted fidelity >98%; coherent quantum information exchange demonstrated

title: Ultra-wideband reflective polarization rotator achieving 104% measured bandwidth with high-efficiency multi-state polarization control
task: Develop ultra-wideband reflective polarization rotator with multi-state conversion capability
key_results: 12.68–38.79 GHz coverage (104% measured bandwidth); linear-to-elliptical/linear/circular conversion; >91% conversion efficiency; stable to 30° oblique incidence
comments: Omega-type bianisotropy from asymmetric octa-circular geometry achieves 104% RBW exceeding typical symmetric designs; excellent theory-experiment concordance.

model_io.model: semi-octa-circular copper metasurface on F4BM220 substrate with ground plane

hypotheses.hypothesis: Rectangular cutout-induced Omega-type bianisotropy extends fractional bandwidth beyond symmetric designs
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: 104% experimental RBW achieved with 91%+ conversion efficiency

title: Directional motion of a self-steering active intruder in a dense crowd of cognitive active agents
task: Study directional navigation of self-steering active intruder through crowd of cognitive active agents
key_results: Intruder speed maximized when agents perceive and avoid in time (not by steering); agent self-steering enhances hyperuniformity (class III), facilitating intruder navigation; maneuverability/vision-angle dependence characterized
comments: Counter-intuitive: intruder steering reduces directional speed; agent perception-driven motion is key enabler; results relevant to emergency personnel in crowds.

model_io.model: overdamped Langevin dynamics of intelligent active Brownian particles (iABPs)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Intruder directional motion maximized when agents perceive and avoid; agent hyperuniformity facilitates navigation
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: intruder steering fails; agent perception-driven avoidance enhances class-III hyperuniformity enabling efficient intruding

title: Investigating the impact of irradiation on various ringFET-based SRAM circuits using 3D TCAD
task: Assess radiation robustness of ringFET-based SRAM under single-event upset exposure using 3D TCAD
key_results: BOX-LDD ringFET SRAM with inner-drain design shows highest critical dose tolerance; improved read/write/hold static noise margins; enhanced radiation robustness vs. junctionless/LDD architectures
comments: Comprehensive 3D TCAD analysis identifies optimal device/layout configuration for aerospace/space applications with severe radiation environment.

model_io.model: ringFET-based 6T SRAM cell (junctionless, LDD, BOX-LDD variants)

hypotheses.hypothesis: BOX-LDD ringFET with inner-drain architecture maximizes critical dose tolerance
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: demonstrates highest radiation robustness and SNM among investigated structures

title: Study on wind resistance performance of high-rise corridor building based on quasi-steady static aeroelastic analysis method
task: Analyze wind-resistant performance of high-rise connected corridor buildings via quasi-steady static aeroelastic CFD-FEM coupling
key_results: Streamlined airfoil profiles and connected corridors reduce inter-story displacement and torsion; static aeroelastic method quantifies peak displacement and torsion under average wind loads
comments: Semi-decoupled CFD-FEM approach with interpolation/rapid reconstruction enables systematic comparison of wind-resistant measures for flexible high-rise structures.

model_io.model: high-rise building with corridor (airfoil/square/elliptical section geometry)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Streamlined airfoil section and connected corridor architecture reduce wind-induced deformation
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: both measures systematically reduce peak displacement and inter-story torsion

title: Numerical investigation and assessment of the Langmuir–Hinshelwood–Hougen–Watson model for dry reforming of methane
task: Assess Langmuir-Hinshelwood-Hougen-Watson kinetic model for dry reforming of methane via plug-flow reactor simulation
key_results: Literature-derived LHHW model qualitatively replicates high/moderate-to-high conversion trends; systematic deviations at low temperatures; high activation energies reflect composite CH4 mechanisms
comments: Diagnostic reanalysis without re-fitting parameters; residual structure analysis identifies operating regimes where model applies; demonstrates mechanistic information extraction.

model_io.model: plug-flow reactor with Ni catalyst for CH4/CO2 dry reforming

hypotheses.hypothesis: Literature-derived LHHW model captures dry reforming kinetics without parameter re-fitting
hypotheses.result: Confirmed for moderate-to-high temperatures; high-activation-energy discrepancy suggests composite elementary steps in CH4 activation

title: Electronic crystals in layered materials
task: Review electronic crystallization phenomena in 2D van der Waals heterostructures
key_results: Electronic crystals identified as prominent phases in moiré superlattices with strong correlations and nontrivial topology; experimental platforms and measurement techniques summarized
comments: Comprehensive review of electron crystallization in graphene and transition-metal dichalcogenides; highlights open questions and future directions for electronic crystal physics.

title: Path-dependent dynamic response in nano graphite membrane resonators under elastic boundary modulation
task: Characterize path-dependent nonlinear dynamics in graphite membrane resonators with elastic boundaries
key_results: Resonance behavior depends on driving amplitude, sweep direction/speed; bifurcations and frequency shifts observed; geometry-dependent nonlinearities in higher modes
comments: Novel identification of dynamic boundary elasticity as hidden degrees of freedom; provides nano-scale friction probing platform.

model_io.model: nano graphite membrane resonator

hypotheses.hypothesis: Elastic van der Waals interfaces govern strain reorganization and nonlinear behavior
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: path-dependent dynamics exhibit bifurcations and frequency shifts dependent on boundary elasticity

title: Synergy drives collective performance in networks
task: Identify synergy as underlying mechanism of collective problem-solving performance in agent networks
key_results: Synergy (not redundancy) predicts group performance across network structures; balancing local redundancy with long-range synergy enables efficient problem-solving; synergy overrides network structure effects
comments: Information-theoretic analysis via Potions Task; synergy mediates network structure effects on collective outcomes—formalizes causal mechanism beyond topology alone.

model_io.model: agent-based Potions Task with iABPs in various network structures (small-world, random, regular)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Synergy in information processing drives collective problem-solving independent of network structure
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: synergy predicts performance even in inefficient network topologies; information-processing synergy is primary driver

title: Waveguide-integrated colour centres in silicon carbide with broadband photonic crystal reflectors for efficient readout
task: Integrate colour centres in silicon carbide waveguides with photonic crystal reflectors for efficient quantum readout
key_results: Broadband photonic crystal reflectance >80% over 60 THz; saturation intensity 103.8±4.2 kcps; readout fidelity >98% predicted with count-rate enhancement to 125 kcps
comments: Cryogenic characterization of integrated devices; tapered-waveguide-fibre interface enables efficient photon collection; spectral stability must improve for high excitation.

model_io.model: 4H-SiC colour centre integrated in waveguide with Dinosaur photonic crystal reflector

hypotheses.hypothesis: Waveguide-integrated colour centres with broadband PC reflectors achieve efficient readout enabling high-fidelity qubit measurement
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: >98% predicted fidelity with optimized count-rate collection schemes
